title: Can you instantiate an abstract class directly (new AbstractClass())? No: but you CAN create an anonymous subclass (new AbstractClass() { ... }). How does this relate to anonymous classes?
shortTitle: Can you instantiate an abstract class?
keyPoints: No: new AbstractClass() is a compile error because abstract classes have unimplemented methods
Yes: new AbstractClass() { implement methods here } creates an anonymous subclass that compiles and runs
The anonymous subclass must implement all abstract methods inline in the curly braces
Lambda expressions (Java 8) replaced anonymous classes for functional interfaces (one abstract method)
Anonymous classes are still needed for abstract classes and interfaces with multiple abstract methods
Anonymous classes have their own this reference and can have instance fields, unlike lambdas

s1_definition.oneliner: new AbstractClass() is a compile error. new AbstractClass() { implement abstract methods here } creates an anonymous subclass. Lambda replaced anonymous for single-method interfaces. Anonymous is still needed for abstract classes and multi-method interfaces.
s1_definition.profdef:
You cannot instantiate an abstract class directly because it has unimplemented methods.

- **Direct instantiation**: `new Account()` on an abstract Account is a compile error.
- **Anonymous subclass**: `new Account("id", balance) { @Override calculateInterest() { return ZERO; } }` creates an unnamed class that extends Account, implements all abstract methods, and is instantiated in one expression.
- **Lambda** (Java 8): replaced anonymous classes for functional interfaces (one abstract method). `(a, b) -> a.compareTo(b)` is shorter than `new Comparator<>() { @Override int compare(...) { ... } }`.
- **Lambda limitation**: lambdas cannot replace anonymous subclasses for abstract classes (which have constructors and fields) or interfaces with multiple abstract methods.
- **Anonymous class features**: has its own `this` reference, can have instance fields, generates a separate `.class` file.
s1_definition.analogy: An abstract class is like a blank form template at National Bank of India. You cannot submit a blank form (cannot instantiate). You must fill in the blanks (implement abstract methods). Anonymous subclass means filling in the blanks right there on the spot. Named subclass means taking the form home (creating a separate class), filling it in, and bringing it back later. Both produce a valid, complete form.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  ABSTRACT CLASS INSTANTIATION
  ──────────────────────────────────────────

  new Account()          -> COMPILE ERROR
  (cannot instantiate abstract)

  new Account() {        -> ANONYMOUS SUBCLASS
    @Override methods()    (compiler generates Main$1.class)
  };

  new SavingsAccount()   -> NAMED SUBCLASS
  (separate .java file)

  LAMBDA vs ANONYMOUS
  ──────────────────────────────────────────
  Functional interface (1 method) -> use lambda
  Abstract class                  -> must use anonymous
  Interface (2+ methods)          -> must use anonymous
  Need instance fields            -> must use anonymous
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
You cannot instantiate an abstract class directly: new Account() is a compile error because abstract classes have unimplemented methods. But you can create an anonymous subclass that provides implementations inline: new Account(id, balance) { @Override calculateInterest() { ... } }. The compiler generates an unnamed class that extends the abstract class, implements all abstract methods, and is instantiated immediately.

Before Java 8, anonymous classes were the primary way to provide on-the-fly implementations. Lambdas (Java 8) replaced this for functional interfaces (one abstract method). But lambdas cannot replace anonymous subclasses for abstract classes (which have constructors, fields, and multiple abstract methods) or interfaces with multiple abstract methods. Anonymous classes are still used in test fixtures, event handlers, and configuration customization.

Remember one sentence: you cannot instantiate an abstract class, but you can create an anonymous subclass inline, and lambdas only replace anonymous classes for functional interfaces with one abstract method.
